credit_ratings.summary: S&P Global Ratings downgraded Spirit Airlines LLC's issuer credit rating to D (default) from CCC after the 2025 Chapter 11 filing; the rating table shows D/--, with no outlook stated.
Fitch downgraded Spirit Airlines' Long-Term Issuer Default Rating to D from CCC- after the second Chapter 11 filing; related senior secured debt was downgraded to C/RR4.

Moody's downgraded Spirit Airlines LLC's corporate family rating to Caa3 from Caa1, its probability of default rating to Caa3-PD from Caa1-PD, and its speculative-grade liquidity rating to SGL-4 from SGL-3; outlook changed to negative from stable.

debt_events.summary: Spirit emerged from its first Chapter 11 case after approximately $795 million of funded debt was equitized; it received a $350 million equity investment, issued $840 million of exit secured notes due 2030, and entered a $275 million exit revolving facility.

Spirit borrowed the entire available $275 million under its exit revolving credit facility; the 2025 Form 10-K says the revolver was fully drawn to fund operations and credit-card collateral requirements.

Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. and five affiliates filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the Southern District of New York, Case No. 25-11897; this was the second Chapter 11 filing in less than a year.

From the petition date, the company ceased making principal and interest payments and ceased accruing interest on long-term debt reclassified as liabilities subject to compromise, subject to bankruptcy-court treatment.

The Bankruptcy Court approved a super-priority DIP facility with aggregate principal capacity up to $1.2 billion, including up to $475 million of new-money loans and up to $750 million of roll-up DIP loans; reported new-money draws were $200 million on October 14, $50 million on November 7, and $100 million on December 15, 2025.

Spirit amended the DIP credit agreement and drew the full $100 million third new-money draw; $50 million net of original-issue discount was immediately available and $50 million was required to remain encumbered pending restructuring or exit-financing progress.

Spirit began an orderly wind-down with all flights cancelled, stating that no additional funding was available and that sustaining the business required hundreds of millions of additional liquidity it could not procure.

payment_behaviour.summary: The 2025 Form 10-K reported $124.4 million of accounts payable within liabilities subject to compromise, representing pre-petition obligations to be resolved through the Chapter 11 process; enforcement of pre-petition liabilities was generally subject to the automatic stay.

Spirit said card-ticket refunds would be processed to the original payment method, while vouchers, credits and Free Spirit points would be addressed later through the bankruptcy process; customer service was no longer available after the shutdown.

distress_signals.summary: Management stated that substantial doubt existed about the company's ability to continue as a going concern within one year from filing the 2025 Form 10-K while the Chapter 11 case remained unresolved.
The 2025 Form 10-K reported a 17.4% reduction in the pilot and flight-attendant workforce from headcount rationalization and restructuring actions.

All flights were cancelled and Spirit entered an immediate orderly wind-down; management attributed the decision to a material rise in oil prices, other business pressures and the absence of additional funding.

Reuters reported that Spirit planned to retain about 150 employees during the wind-down and reduce headcount to about 40 after the first three months; CFO Fred Comer said there was no viable path to continued operations.

ownership.value: Publicly held Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. with dispersed institutional ownership immediately before the shutdown: as of 2026-04-15, the largest disclosed 5% holders included PIMCO (9.5%), Arena Capital Advisors (9.1%), AllianceBernstein (8.4%), Cyrus Capital (7.6%), Ares Management (7.0%), M&G (6.5%) and Citadel (5.7%). The entity had changed its name from Spirit Airlines, Inc. on 2025-03-13; after the 2026-05-02 wind-down, the bankruptcy estate and court-supervised process—not a verified single sponsor—control remaining assets, and common-stock holders were told to expect a complete loss.
ownership.as_of: 2026-04-15 for the last verified beneficial-ownership table; wind-down began 2026-05-02

output.risk_rationale: Risk is high: the exact SEC filer reported $3.797 billion of FY2025 operating revenue but separate successor and predecessor operating losses, only $273.0 million of unrestricted cash, $1.259 billion of reported long-term debt and another $1.609 billion of debt in liabilities subject to compromise, while management stated substantial doubt about going concern. S&P and Fitch moved the issuer to D after the second Chapter 11 filing, and Moody's had Caa3 with a negative outlook before that filing. Spirit then reported that it had no additional funding and began an immediate wind-down on 2026-05-02, so ordinary obligations are being handled in a court-supervised liquidation rather than by an operating airline.
